summary: Read-only: find HBM/VRAM footprint reductions with ZERO quality loss across the 3 megakernels (workspace sizing, recompute-vs-store, per-CTA grad scratch, smem->HBM, dispatch scratch) to enable bigger batch/model

ranked.where: csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:463-465 (mb_tc_looksam_floats=2*kMambaTotalElems, summed unconditionally at :517), fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:582-585 (dec_tc_looksam_floats, summed at :635 inside dec_tc_staged_opt_floats), fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:455-458 (vit_tc_looksam_floats). opt_id is ALREADY a launcher param (mega_mamba_...launcher.cu:99, mega_decoder_...launcher.cu:108, mega_vit_...launcher.cu:75) but is NOT threaded into the *_tc_workspace_floats sizers (mega_mamba:115, mega_decoder:123, mega_vit:88).
ranked.change: Thread opt_id into the three *_tc_workspace_floats functions; make *_tc_looksam_floats return 0 unless opt_id in {LookSAM(4), SuperGrok11, SuperGrok15, SuperGrok2}. The kernel's P2.4 consumer is already `if constexpr(Opt==LookSAM||SG11||SG15||SG2)` (fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:712-713), so the region is dead for every other Opt. The decoder already has the exact precedent: dec_tc_looksam_floats returns 0 at bench width via `if(!kDecStagedOptScratch)` (:583) — generalize that gate from compile-time-bench to runtime-opt_id.
ranked.bytes_saved: 2*total*4 B per model on every non-SAM step (the production AdamW/Lion/Grokfast/Prodigy/Muon/NeuralGrok/GrokAdamW path). d=128: mamba 4.75 MB + decoder 3.38 MB + vit 3.34 MB = ~11.5 MB. At 1.5B params: 2*1.5e9*4 = 12 GB per model, ~36 GB across the 3 models per step.
ranked.gate_note: The carved region is never read on non-SAM Opts (P2.4 if-constexpr'd out), so shrinking it to 0 leaves every byte the kernel touches at the same workspace offset (looksam is carved AFTER opt_reduce and the regions after it — muon/sg2 — are themselves opt-gated to 0 on the same path, so no live offset shifts). Confirm by PTX-diff of the AdamW kernel instantiation (unchanged) + a workspace-offset assert; A/A/A bit-identical run on adamw.

ranked.id: MB-WS-1 / M0 — Mamba projection-grad output-stationary dW (the 668 GB OOM wall)
ranked.where: csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:514 (nCTA*kMambaTotalElems FULL per-CTA grad partial), zeroed P0 :608, accumulated P1 :628 via mb_backward_sample, cross-CTA reduced P2 :643-652 (`acc += part_base[c*total_p+off+i]`). Root grad write is mb_linear_bwd model_stage_mamba3.cuh:451 (`dW[o*in_dim+i] += acc` into the CTA-private g=mb_bind_grad(my_part)). PERF_ANALYSIS.md M0 (projections=94% of FLOPs at 1.5B) + corrections #2/#3. Decoder proven pattern: model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:2175-2176 (`grad[sp.grad_off+m*Kin+n0+n]=v`).
ranked.change: Adopt the decoder output-stationary dW for the four PROJECTION weights (in_proj, x_proj, dt_proj, out_proj) which dominate params at scale: tile each dW by weight-element ownership, contract the batch dimension as the GEMM K, write grad[off+...] directly — eliminating the per-CTA full copy + the cross-CTA reduce for those tensors. Replace nCTA*kMambaTotalElems with O(nCTA*tile-scratch) for the projection share. (The scan-coupled per-head/head-shared params still need a small reduce, but they are a tiny share of total at scale.)
ranked.bytes_saved: Removes ~(nCTA-1)/nCTA = 131/132 = 99.2% of the dominant term. d=128 production: 313 MB -> a few hundred MB tile scratch. At 1.5B: ~792 GB (PERF_ANALYSIS cites ~668 GB for its effective P) -> hundreds of MB. This is the single largest VRAM term in the codebase and a HARD OOM (H100=80 GB) precondition for any d>=1024/1.5B Mamba.
ranked.gate_note: NOT byte-identical: batch is summed in weight-tile (GEMM-K) order instead of the per-sample then ascending-CTA order, so fp32 reassociation differs at fp32-ULP. PERF_ANALYSIS M0 marks the substrate SAFE (proven decoder pattern, ascending-k, owner-computes dW, scan untouched). Gate: fp64 oracle parity HARD-gate at 1e-4 + A/A/A determinism (deterministic tile ownership keeps it run-to-run identical) per the patch-protocol ratchet; the scan backward math is unchanged so only the projection-dW reduction order moves.

ranked.id: MB-SMEM-M1 — Mamba activations->HBM one layer at a time (d=2048 placement unblock)
ranked.where: csrc/fused/sm_90/mamba3_layout.cuh:270-278 (production kMambaSmemBytes=215844 ~211 KB at d=128; cap assert <=228*1024 at :275-278) and bench placeholder :158-159 (1,317,924 B ~1.29 MB at d=1024). MambaSampleSmem caches BOTH layers' fwd acts+adjoints, all d-scaled (model_stage_mamba3.cuh:155-192). Occ<1 -> launcher REFUSES at fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:1259 (and the occ probe at :1226-1229). PERF_ANALYSIS M1 (~2.5 MB needed vs 227 KB cap).
ranked.change: Stream forward activations to HBM one layer at a time and recompute/read-back in the backward, keeping only the current layer's working set resident, instead of caching both layers at once. The struct already partial-recomputes (xhat recomputed in bwd, not cached); extend that to per-layer eviction so live smem drops below the 227 KB opt-in cap and d=2048 places at occ=1.
ranked.bytes_saved: Does not shrink the (fixed per-SM) smem itself, but is the gating ENABLER: without it Mamba is hard-pinned to d=128 (cannot place at d=2048 at all). Trades a per-layer HBM activation buffer (small vs the 792 GB grad term) for crossing the placement cap. Pairs with MB-WS-1 as the two preconditions for d=2048/1.5B Mamba.
ranked.gate_note: The forward is deterministic with a fixed register-resident seq=8 scan (model_stage_mamba3.cuh:52-62), so recompute reads bit-identical activations. Gate: A/A/A determinism + fp64 parity unchanged (recompute reproduces the exact stored values); verify occ>=1 at d=2048 via the cudaOccupancy probe at :1226.

Writes use rcls=si*kSeq (line 971) at :980/:983 — only kSamplesPerTile=64 distinct rows of kTileM=1088 are ever written; bwd reads same sparse rcls at :1162/:1169/:1175. ranked.where: csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:648-654 (dec_tc_dw_transpose_floats, carve-LAST), model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:144-145 (default SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1), :1994 (kDecDwTransposeActive=(kDecDwStage==1)&&(kDecDwSplitK==1)), :2058-2059 / :2090 (the transpose pass + scalar fallback). dec_dw_run_tile (:2175-2176) feeds the identical wgmma issue sequence on both paths.

synth.notes:
HIGHEST-LEVERAGE SCALE-ENABLER: MB-WS-1 / M0 (csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:514 + model_stage_mamba3.cuh:451). The per-CTA FULL flat-grad partial (nCTA*kMambaTotalElems fp32, P0:608 -> P1:628 -> P2 reduce:643-652) is ~792 GB at 1.5B vs an 80 GB H100 -- a HARD OOM (PERF_ANALYSIS.md correction #3, ~668 GB for its effective P) that blocks ALL 1B+ Mamba. Adopting the proven decoder output-stationary dW (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:2175-2176) for the projection weights -- which PERF_ANALYSIS M0 shows are 94% of FLOPs/params at scale -- removes 131/132=99.2% of the single largest VRAM term in the codebase. Paired with M1 (acts->HBM one layer at a time, mamba3_layout.cuh:275 cap) it is the precondition for d=2048/1.5B Mamba to place and run at all. Both ride the same fp64-gated ratchet.

QUALITY-CLASS CORRECTION the two conflicting Mamba items force: this is tolerance-bounded, NOT byte-identical (MB-WS-1/MB-GRAD-PARTIAL's 'recompute-bit-identical' label is wrong) and NOT infeasible (mamba-full-grad-partial-fp32's 'RISKY/no zero-loss change exists' is too pessimistic). Going output-stationary reassociates the batch sum into GEMM-K order, which differs from the current per-sample->ascending-CTA fp32 order at fp32-ULP -> must clear the 1e-4 fp64 gate (it will: same math, only reduction order moves; PERF_ANALYSIS marks the substrate SAFE). The bf16-PARTIAL fallback (MB-WS-4 / the bf16 variant in mamba-full-grad-partial-fp32) IS correctly RISKY and strictly inferior -- list it only as a fallback if the rewrite is deferred; do not pursue it as a primary.

FREE TIER (do these first, single host-side change, byte-identical, no kernel edit): opt_id is ALREADY a launcher parameter (mega_{mamba,decoder,vit}_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:99/108/75) but is NOT passed into the *_tc_workspace_floats sizers. Threading it through and returning 0 from the looksam/sg2/muon carves on the non-matching Opt (all four staged-opt regions consumed under if-constexpr already, decoder has the exact !kDecStagedOptScratch precedent) reclaims on the production AdamW path: ~11.5 MB (looksam) + ~3.1 GB decoder + structural mamba/vit (sg2, ~199 GB at d=1024) + ~6.6 MB (muon) at d=128, scaling to tens of GB at 1.5B. The sg2 gate specifically is what lets the d=1024 non-SG2 bench build (documented OOM at model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:596-608). LION-V (10 GB/model at 1.5B) and VIT-01 (~66 MB) are the next byte-identical wins. Confirm each by PTX-diffing the affected Opt's kernel instantiation (must be unchanged) + a workspace-offset assert, then one A/A/A bit-identical run.

RISKY (separate note, do NOT ship without a passing 1e-4 gate): VIT-03 (n1x/n2x LN-xhat -> bf16, ~140 MB) -- the LN bwd correction dx=iv*(dxhat-(sda+xhr*sdax)/D) at model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:753 amplifies xhat precision (xhat enters twice: dgw at :737 and sdax at :746), higher sensitivity than attn; verified the amplification is real. VIT-02 (attn weights -> bf16, ~39 MB) is milder (17-term softmax-dot into fp32 accum) and likely within tol but still not bit-identical. MB-WS-4 (grad partials bf16). PRODIGY-PARAM-INIT-BF16. All four are tolerance-bounded reductions gated on fp64 parity, not zero-loss in the byte/recompute sense.

NOT a free win (flagged so it is not mistaken for one): decoder-dw-transpose-staging (SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=0, ~139 MB) is bit-identical but trades a 2.05x dW-GEMM slowdown for the VRAM -- KEEP only if the freed memory enables a larger B/d that nets faster on the 3-seed timing ratchet. decoder-c1t-transposed-weight-cache (~201 MB at d=2048) is the same perf<->VRAM trade (~14% dX slowdown). FUSEDSCRATCH-ACTS-GFX942 is HIP-path-only (sm_90 never instantiates FusedScratch -- dispatch.cpp:413 acts=zeros_like(params) + per-step zero_() at :441), relevant only for gfx942.
